resources.string: Tickory works with your own server. Enter the address you use to open Tickory in your browser.
Note: with http the connection is not encrypted. Only use this on your own home network.
Enter the address of your server.
The address must start with https:// or http://.
Don\'t put a username or password in the address. You sign in afterwards, in the app.
This is not a valid address. Check it for typos.
This address could not be found. Check the address and your internet connection.
Can\'t connect to the server. Check the address and make sure the server is running. Is the server at home? Then check that you are connected to your own Wi-Fi.
The server is not responding. Check the address and your connection, then try again.
The secure connection failed: the server\'s certificate is not trusted.
Does your server run at home without https? Then put http:// in front of the address; that is only allowed for an address on your own network.
An address with http:// is only allowed on your own network (for example 192.168.1.10 or nas.local). A server on the internet needs https://, otherwise your password and sign-in travel unencrypted.

The configured address uses http:// for a server outside your own network. Tickory no longer connects to it, because your password and sign-in would travel unencrypted. Change the server address and use https://.
There is no Tickory server at this address (response %1$d).
This address redirects to %1$s. Enter that address if it is your server.
This address redirects to another address. Enter the address your server actually runs on.
Your server is on your own network. Android asks for the ‘Nearby devices’ permission for that. Tickory only uses it to reach your own server.
Without this permission Tickory can\'t reach your server on the home network. You can grant it in the app\'s settings, under Permissions › Nearby devices.
Is your server on your home network? Then Tickory needs the ‘Nearby devices’ permission.
Tickory can\'t reach %1$s. Check your internet connection and make sure the server is running.
The server at %1$s returned an error (%2$d).
The secure connection to %1$s failed: the server\'s certificate is not trusted.
The server redirects the app to %1$s. Tickory only opens the address you have set. Has your server moved? Then change the server address.
You will be signed out on this device and the scheduled reminders will be removed. Changes that have not been sent to the server yet will be lost.
No app was found to open this link.
Tickory needs the Android component ‘Android System WebView’, but it is missing or turned off.
Notifications for the reminders on your tasks
No connection. The task will be completed as soon as there is a connection again.
Completing failed: the task no longer exists or you no longer have access to it.
Completing failed. Open the app to try it there.
You have been signed out. Open the app and sign in again to complete this task.
Completing failed: the server can\'t be reached. Open the app to try again.
What is overdue and what is due today. Tap the circle to complete.
The open tasks of a project, the Inbox, Today or Upcoming. You choose when you place it.
The next two weeks, by day.
A button that opens Tickory on the Add task window.
Sign in again via the app
Nothing planned for the next two weeks
This project is gone. Choose another project.
Filters cannot be shown in a widget yet. Choose a project.
Sign in via the app to see your projects here. You can already choose Today, Upcoming and Inbox.
You are signed out. Sign in again to fetch the attachment.
This attachment no longer exists on the server.
This attachment is too large to fetch.
The attachment could not be fetched. Check your connection and try again.
No app was found to open this file. Choose Save and open it yourself.
